name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,695

clue.text: Ready to introduce simple woollen fabric

indicators.note: to introduce something is to come before it, so the first word's letters lead the second's

blocks.note: ready money, or the readies, is cash
mere means simple or nothing more than

explanation.surface: A plain fabric is about to be launched on the market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' reads as an adjective, but here it is the noun for money, as in 'the ready'.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is a fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, woven into luxury cloth.

clue.text: Note Conservative meeting Chief Medical Officer, scratching head

indicators.note: scratching out the head of a word removes its first letter

blocks.note: C is the standard abbreviation for Conservative
Chris Whitty was England's Chief Medical Officer through the Covid pandemic

explanation.surface: A Tory politician sits down with the government's chief doctor and is handed a memo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' sits at the start looking like a musical note to be turned into letters, but it is the definition. The Chief Medical Officer is a person here, not an abbreviation such as CMO.
explanation.definitionFit: A chitty is an informal British word for a short written memo, voucher or receipt.

clue.text: Emaciated-looking broadcaster hosting international news

indicators.note: a host takes guests inside, so one set of letters is held within another

blocks.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster
I is the abbreviation for international
N stands for new, and news is read as its plural, two lots of N

explanation.surface: A gaunt newsreader presents the world headlines.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is the British satellite TV company, a common crossword broadcaster; 'news' is treated playfully as 'new' twice, each giving N.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny describes someone very thin, close to the wasted look of an emaciated person.

clue.text: Humiliation essentially stops Warren becoming a grass

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its core, so only its central letter is kept
a stopper plugs a gap from inside, so one piece sits within another

blocks.note: a warren is a confusing network of passages, like a labyrinth
the sixth of eleven letters is the centre

explanation.surface: Shame makes a rabbit warren end up overgrown.
explanation.walkthrough: Warren with a capital looks like a person's name; it is a maze of burrows.
explanation.definitionFit: Maize, or corn, is botanically a cereal grass, as are wheat and barley.

clue.text: Appreciate what Madame Tussauds' waxworks are lacking reportedly?

indicators.note: a report is something passed on by voice, so the sound counts here rather than the spelling

blocks.clueFragment: what Madame Tussauds' waxworks are lacking
blocks.note: wax figures have glass eyes, not living ones

explanation.surface: A question about what the wax figures at Madame Tussauds are missing.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame Tussauds is the London waxworks museum; its models have glass eyes, so they lack 'real eyes', which said aloud is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate a fact is to understand or become aware of it fully, which is to grasp it.

clue.text: Republican wearing skimpy beachwear generates crowd

indicators.note: clothing goes around its wearer, so one piece is wrapped by another

blocks.note: a thong is a very skimpy swimsuit bottom
R is the abbreviation for Republican

explanation.surface: An American politician in a tiny swimsuit draws a mob of onlookers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Generates' is just the link: the wordplay produces the answer, which then means the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A throng is a large densely packed mass of people, the same as a crowd.

clue.text: Snuggle round rather novel fireside feature

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters are made into a new order
to go round something is to enclose it on both sides

blocks.note: to snuggle up is to hug
taken as written

explanation.surface: Curling up with a good book by the fire sounds cosy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as a book to curl up with; it is an adjective meaning new, and signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A hearthrug is the mat laid in front of a fireplace, a typical item of the fireside.

clue.text: Half of football team, extremely engaged and aligned

indicators.note: taking half of a two-word name drops one of its words entirely
the extremes of a word are its two ends, so only the outer letters stay

blocks.note: Leyton Orient is a London football club; the second half of its name is kept
first and last letters

explanation.surface: Half a football side is fully committed and lined up together.
explanation.walkthrough: Leyton Orient is a football club in east London, often reduced to its second word in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Oriented means positioned or directed a particular way, so something lined up in one direction.

clue.text: Reports of firearms produced by thugs son abused

indicators.note: something abused is mistreated and knocked out of shape, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bangs are heard after a gang mistreats a boy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reports' here means loud bangs, not written accounts.
explanation.definitionFit: A report is the sharp bang of a gun being fired, so reports of firearms are the shots heard.

clue.text: Antagonistic criminal claiming over one grand's been stolen

indicators.note: something stolen is taken away, so a letter is removed
over can mean on top of or in addition to, so one piece is added to another
something criminal is bent or crooked, so the letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: the word with its grand removed
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crook insists that more than a thousand pounds has been stolen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like the person doing the claiming, but it is the signal to rearrange; G for grand is lifted out of CLAIMING and I for one added.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means hostile or unfriendly, so the word describes someone acting as an adversary.

clue.text: Virtually delighted to find unit for measuring angles

indicators.note: virtually means almost, so the word is not quite complete and loses its last letter

blocks.note: radiant means beaming with joy

explanation.surface: A student is almost thrilled to discover how angles are measured.
explanation.walkthrough: Radiant, glowing with happiness, loses its final T.
explanation.definitionFit: A radian is the SI unit of angle, the angle subtended at a circle's centre by an arc equal to its radius.

clue.text: Banker, upset, suppresses fury he's getting sacked

indicators.note: someone sacked is dismissed and leaves, so those letters drop out
to upset something is to tip it over, so in a down clue the letters run back up

blocks.note: to seethe is to be inwardly furious without letting it out
taken as written, then removed

explanation.surface: A banker, rattled, bottles up his rage as he faces the sack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' is a crossword trick for a river, something with banks; the Tees flows through north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: A river has banks along both sides, so in crossword language any river can be called a banker.

clue.text: Fruit fly, back near fiancé every so often

indicators.note: going back means travelling the other way, so the letters are read right to left
doing something every so often means at intervals, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: a gnat is a small fly
the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A fruit fly buzzes back beside someone's husband-to-be.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fruit fly' reads as one insect, but the comma splits them: fruit is the definition and the fly is a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small loose-skinned citrus, a kind of mandarin orange.

clue.text: Swimmer from school having change of heart

indicators.note: a change of heart swaps the central letter for a different one

blocks.note: to school someone is to teach them
the replacement centre letter

explanation.surface: A swimmer leaving school has a change of mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'School' looks like a noun, a building or a shoal of fish; it is the verb 'to teach', whose middle A becomes N.
explanation.definitionFit: A tench is a freshwater fish of the carp family, and crosswords often call any fish a swimmer.

clue.text: Length of metal, tungsten, about to carry current

indicators.note: to carry something is to hold it within, so a letter is placed inside

blocks.note: W is the chemical symbol for tungsten
re means about or concerning
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A strip of tungsten is about to carry an electric current.
explanation.walkthrough: W for tungsten comes from its old name wolfram.
explanation.definitionFit: A wire is a long thin flexible thread of drawn metal, cut to whatever length is needed.

clue.text: Stupidity concealed by sovereign or ancestors?

indicators.note: something concealed by other words lies inside them, waiting to be read out

blocks.note: the run of letters across the three words

explanation.surface: A wry question whether a monarch's foolishness was inherited from the royal line.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the surface is a tease: the answer runs from the end of 'sovereign' through 'or' into 'ancestors'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignorance is a lack of knowledge, close enough to stupidity in loose everyday use.

clue.text: Musical instrument, extravagant present?

indicators.note: extravagant means wild and unrestrained, so the letters run wild into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Is a musical instrument an over-the-top gift?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extravagant present' reads as a lavish gift; the adjective is the anagram signal. The serpent is an obscure old bass wind instrument shaped like a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The serpent is a curved Renaissance bass wind instrument with a cup mouthpiece, an ancestor of the tuba.

clue.text: US lawman that is caught with electronic listening device

blocks.note: Wyatt Earp was a famous Wild West marshal
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is
C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught
E is the abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail

explanation.surface: An American sheriff is caught carrying a bugging device.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caught' looks like part of the story of the lawman; it is just the letter C from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: An earpiece is the small speaker worn in the ear, a device for listening to sound.

clue.text: Overjoyed still after case of cybercrime is overturned

indicators.note: the case of something is its outer shell, so only the first and last letters are kept
turned over means flipped, so the pair is read the other way
after places one piece behind another in the order of reading

blocks.note: first and last letters
static means motionless, still

explanation.surface: Someone is still delighted after an online-fraud case is thrown out on appeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' and 'overturned' suggest a court judgment being reversed; both are mechanical instructions.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecstatic means in a state of intense joy, the same delight as being overjoyed.

clue.text: Ultimately terrific article probing a strange mystery

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter is taken
a probe goes into something, so these letters are pushed inside another word

blocks.note: taken as written
rum is old British slang for odd or strange
the final letter
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A wonderful newspaper piece investigates a puzzling unsolved case.
explanation.walkthrough: Rum, meaning odd, is old-fashioned British slang; CAN is pushed between its R and UM.
explanation.definitionFit: An arcanum is a deep secret or hidden piece of knowledge, especially one known only to initiates.

clue.text: Brother married Greek, finally keeping old name

indicators.note: finally points to the end, so only the last letter counts
to keep something is to hold it inside, so a pair of letters goes within

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for married
its final letter
O is the abbreviation for old
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A man wed a Greek woman and in the end kept his old surname.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brother' looks like a family member at a wedding; it means a member of a religious order.
explanation.definitionFit: Monks are addressed as Brother, the title used for members of a male religious community.

clue.text: Spanish city force to scrap uniform requirement primarily

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken
to scrap something is to throw it away, so those letters are removed

blocks.note: vigour is strength or force
U is Uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A Spanish city's police drop their rule on wearing uniform.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Force' reads as the police; it means vigour, from which U and R are scrapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Vigo is a port city in Galicia, north-west Spain, on the Atlantic coast.

clue.text: Very angry about boxer's debut in ring

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the first letter is used
about means around, so one word wraps round a letter

blocks.note: V is the abbreviation for very
irate means angry
its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone is furious about a fighter's first bout in the boxing ring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like the boxing ring of the surface, but it is a verb, to resonate like a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: A bell or glass rings because it is shaking rapidly, so to ring is to resonate with quick oscillation.

clue.text: Dishonest account, rued to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent means partly, so only part of the following words is used

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: A false story is something its teller partly regrets.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma after 'account' is ignored; the letters run straight on into the next word.
explanation.definitionFit: Untrue means false or not faithful to the facts, as a deceitful statement is.

clue.text: Beverage Gwyn perhaps picked up for engineer

indicators.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it, so the words count for how they are spoken

blocks.note: a brew is a drink such as tea; Nell Gwyn was Charles II's actress mistress

explanation.surface: A drink, possibly for a Welsh-named woman, is fetched for an engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perhaps' marks Gwyn as an example: her first name is wanted. Isambard Kingdom Brunel was the great Victorian engineer of the Great Western Railway.
explanation.definitionFit: Brunel built bridges, tunnels, ships and railways, making him Britain's most celebrated Victorian civil engineer.

clue.text: Fellow describing time in prison cell

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round it, so one word goes around a letter

blocks.note: a peer is an equal or fellow
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An inmate tells of his time behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Describing' is used in its geometry sense of drawing round. Peter is old British criminal slang for a cell, and also for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: In old British underworld slang a peter is a prison cell, as well as a safe.

clue.text: Bar Ronnie refurbished, easy decision to take

indicators.note: refurbishing something remakes it, so these letters are rebuilt in a fresh order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ronnie doing up his pub was an obvious call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' looks like a verb meaning prohibit; it is the pub being refurbished.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-brainer is an informal term for a choice so obvious it needs no thought at all.

clue.text: Maybe Guardian point of view that's promoting extremism originally

indicators.note: originally means at the start, so only the first letter is kept
promoting moves something up, so a letter is lifted out of its place

blocks.note: an angle is a viewpoint or slant
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A newspaper's opinion line accused of pushing radical views.
explanation.walkthrough: The italics make Guardian the newspaper, but it is a guardian angel; the E at the end of ANGLE is moved up one place in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A guardian angel is one kind of angel, so the definition gives an example with 'maybe'.

clue.text: Increase offer

blocks.note: first meaning: to make larger or longer
second meaning: to hold out, as with an invitation or welcome

explanation.walkthrough: Both words look like nouns, as in a pay increase and a job offer; both are verbs here.
explanation.definitionFit: You extend a building to enlarge it, and you extend an invitation or thanks when you hold them out to someone.

clue.text: Rhona regularly squeezes misshapen orange sponge

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept
misshapen means bent out of its proper form, so the letters are rearranged
squeezing something holds it tight inside, so letters are placed within

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rhona keeps squeezing a lopsided orange as if it were a bath sponge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sponge' looks like a bath sponge to squeeze, but it is a person who sponges off others.
explanation.definitionFit: A sponge in slang is a parasite living off others, which is exactly what a hanger-on does.

clue.text: Bishop leaves Suffolk town for Greater Manchester one

indicators.note: when someone leaves, they go away, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: Beccles is a market town in Suffolk, eastern England
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A bishop moves from one English town to take up a post in another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One' stands for 'town' carried over from the clue, so the definition is a Greater Manchester town; it is famous for Eccles cakes.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccles is a town west of Manchester city centre, within the Greater Manchester county area.

clue.text: Confusedly, game once having Europeans replacing Americans

indicators.note: replacing means putting one thing in another's place, so letters are swapped

blocks.note: pall-mall was an old mallet-and-ball game, giving London's Pall Mall its name
E is the abbreviation for European, one per swap
A is the abbreviation for American, the letters swapped out

explanation.surface: A muddled account of an old sport that swapped its American players for European ones.
explanation.walkthrough: Pall-mall was a seventeenth-century game, like croquet, played down an alley; each A becomes an E.
explanation.definitionFit: Pell-mell means in a disorderly rush, headlong and in confusion.
